metadata.title: NorCal Chinese Food Map
metadata.subtitle: The good stuff — curated by Justin Suo

restaurants.name: Mister Jiu's
restaurants.known_for: Modernized Cantonese banquet — roast duck, salt-and-pepper crab, hand-pulled noodles. Michelin star.
restaurants.vibe: Reservation-required upstairs dining room over Chinatown. The most ambitious Chinese restaurant in NorCal.
tips: Reserve the back patio in summer
The whole duck feeds 4 — order ahead
Cocktail program is destination-level too

restaurants.name: Z & Y Restaurant
restaurants.known_for: Chongqing chicken, dan dan noodles, mapo tofu. Old-school Sichuan, full numbing heat.
restaurants.vibe: Loud, busy, no-frills. The benchmark for SF Sichuan.
restaurants.signature_dish: Mr. Fish in flaming chili oil
tips: Chongqing chicken is the lifeline order
Heat is real Sichuan numbing — bring water
Avoid Friday night rush

restaurants.name: R&G Lounge
restaurants.known_for: Salt and pepper crab. Just order it. Also clay pot, hot stone scallops.
restaurants.vibe: Two-story Chinatown stalwart. Locals on weeknights, banquets on weekends.
tips: Call ahead to reserve a live tank crab — they sell out
Two stories — upstairs is quieter
Banquet menu is great for groups of 6+

restaurants.name: Yank Sing
restaurants.known_for: Shanghai-style xiao long bao, Peking duck, Shanghai dumplings. Cart-style.
restaurants.vibe: Polished, expensive, weekday business lunch crowd. The premium SF dim sum.
tips: Stevenson location is bigger, less wait than Rincon
Brunch reservations book a week out
Cart service makes ordering visual — point at what you want

restaurants.name: Hong Kong Lounge II
restaurants.known_for: Pineapple buns with BBQ pork (cha siu bao), shrimp dumplings, custard buns.
restaurants.vibe: Long weekend waits. Worth it. Sister restaurant to the original on Geary.
dishes: Pineapple cha siu bao (BBQ pork pineapple buns)
tips: Weekend wait is brutal — go Tuesday or Wednesday lunch
The pineapple bun is the photo dish, but har gow is the technical test
Cash + card both fine

restaurants.name: King of Noodles
restaurants.known_for: Hand-pulled noodles, scallion pancakes, dumplings. Cheap and sharp.
restaurants.vibe: Tiny, busy, wait at the door. Cash-friendly.
tips: Cash preferred
Tiny — expect to wait 20 min for a table at lunch
Dumplings are made in-house — order them

restaurants.name: San Tung
restaurants.known_for: Dry-fried chicken wings — the dish that built its name. Also hand-shaved noodles.
restaurants.vibe: Always a line. Plan around it.
tips: The wings are why people line up — order 16 if you have 2+ people
Korean-Chinese hybrid menu — try the jajangmyeon
Lunch line shorter than dinner

restaurants.name: Spices! II
restaurants.known_for: Explosive chili oil dishes, fish in flaming chili oil, mouth-numbing chicken.
restaurants.vibe: Dim, loud, no-pretense. Order with caution if you don't tolerate Sichuan heat.
tips: Ask for 'American spicy' if you can't take Sichuan numbing
Bring cold drinks — bottles only beat the heat
Order rice — you'll need it

restaurants.name: Old Mandarin Islamic
restaurants.known_for: Lamb in everything — lamb hot pot, lamb skewers, hand-pulled noodles, sesame bread.
restaurants.vibe: Halal Muslim Chinese (Hui cuisine). One of a kind in SF.
tips: Halal — no pork on menu
Bring people — order family-style hot pot
One of the only Hui Muslim Chinese spots in NorCal

restaurants.name: Kingdom of Dumpling
restaurants.known_for: Pork XLB (xiao long bao), pan-fried pork buns, scallion pancake.
restaurants.vibe: Cash-only, blink-and-miss-it storefront. Get the take-home frozen dumplings.
tips: Cash only
Take home a bag of frozen XLB — best in city
Blink and you'll miss the storefront

restaurants.name: Shanghai Dumpling King
restaurants.known_for: XLB, pan-fried pork buns, beef noodle soup. Shanghai street food.
restaurants.vibe: Lines out the door on weekends. Mostly takeout.
tips: Lines weekends — call ahead for pickup
Mostly takeout-oriented
Don't expect ambience — go for the dough

restaurants.name: Ton Kiang
restaurants.known_for: Hakka cuisine — salt-baked chicken, stuffed tofu, dim sum on weekends.
restaurants.vibe: One of the few Hakka spots in SF. Family-run since 1977.
tips: One of the only Hakka spots in SF
Try the Hakka stuffed tofu — distinct cuisine you won't find elsewhere
Family-run since 1977

restaurants.name: Shan Dong Restaurant
restaurants.known_for: Hand-pulled noodles, fried dumplings, mu shu pork. Dough is made fresh in the window.
restaurants.vibe: Old-school Oakland Chinatown classic. Cheap, fast, packed.
dishes: Hand-pulled noodles (watch them stretch dough in window)
tips: Cash works — they take card too
Cheap and packed at lunch
Watch through the window before you sit — they pull noodles by hand on demand

restaurants.name: Gum Kuo Restaurant
restaurants.known_for: Congee, chow fun, rice plates. The neighborhood breakfast spot.
restaurants.vibe: Open early, packed at 8am with regulars.
restaurants.signature_dish: Congee with century egg + lean pork
tips: Open early — old-timers' breakfast spot
Comfort food, not destination food
Cheap and consistent

restaurants.name: China Village
restaurants.known_for: Dry-cooked string beans, ma po tofu, fish-fragrant eggplant, smoked tea duck.
restaurants.vibe: Berkeley/Albany Sichuan reference point. Some claim it's the best in the East Bay.
tips: Worth the trip from anywhere in the East Bay
Street parking on Solano — plan extra time
Many claim this is the best Sichuan in the East Bay

restaurants.name: Daimo Chinese Restaurant
restaurants.known_for: Roast duck, char siu, soy sauce chicken, BBQ over rice. Hong Kong-style siu mei.
restaurants.vibe: Pacific East Mall food court vibe. Get the BBQ combo.
restaurants.signature_dish: BBQ combo (roast duck + char siu + crispy pork)
dishes: BBQ combo (roast duck + char siu + crispy pork)
tips: Pacific East Mall food court vibe — fast and cheap
BBQ combo over rice is the move
Skip the seafood, come for the rotisserie

restaurants.name: Great China
restaurants.known_for: Peking duck (must be ordered ahead), double-cooked pork, walnut prawns, dry-fried green beans.
restaurants.vibe: Cal student dinner classic. Founded 1962. The duck is the order — takes 24 hr notice.
tips: Reservations essential
Order Peking duck WHEN YOU BOOK — won't be available walk-in
Founded 1962. Cal alumni dinner ritual

restaurants.name: Imperial Tea Court
restaurants.known_for: Gong-fu tea service paired with dim sum. Small plates, jiaozi, scallion pancakes.
restaurants.vibe: Tea ceremony focus. Quiet, slow, contemplative.
tips: Slow and contemplative — not for rushed groups
Tea is the main event — order a flight
Tucked inside Emeryville Public Market

restaurants.name: Koi Palace
restaurants.known_for: Top-tier dim sum. Lobster XLB, BBQ pork buns, har gow done right. Off-menu specials.
restaurants.vibe: Banquet-hall scale, weekend wait can hit 90 min. The Bay Area dim sum benchmark.
tips: Reservations essential — wait without is 90+ min on weekends
Ask the captain for off-menu items — there's a hidden menu
Bay Area dim sum benchmark

restaurants.name: Hong Kong Flower Lounge
restaurants.known_for: Cantonese banquet — Peking duck, lobster two ways, Maine lobster noodles.
restaurants.vibe: White tablecloths, big lazy susans. Wedding banquet energy.
dishes: Lobster two ways (with noodles, then meat)
tips: Order lobster set, share family-style
Banquet hall scale — great for 8-12 people
Wedding banquets are common — call to check booking conflicts

restaurants.name: The Kitchen
restaurants.known_for: Live seafood tank, salt and pepper soft shell crab, dim sum on weekends.
restaurants.vibe: Loud, fluorescent, packed. Worth the chaos.
restaurants.signature_dish: Salt and pepper soft shell crab
dishes: Salt and pepper soft shell crab
tips: Loud chaos — bring patient company
Live tank — point at what you want
Soft shell crab is the destination dish

restaurants.name: Asian Pearl Seafood
restaurants.known_for: Live tank seafood. Lobster e-fu noodles, salt and pepper Dungeness, abalone.
restaurants.vibe: Banquet-style Cantonese. Order big, share.
tips: Order family-style — banquet portions
Live tank is the move
Bring a group — solo not the play here

restaurants.name: Royal Feast
restaurants.known_for: Beijing-style — sliced lamb, sesame pancakes, hand-shaved noodles, dumplings.
restaurants.vibe: Slightly upscale Northern Chinese. Less Cantonese crowd.
dishes: Beijing sliced lamb (with sesame paste dipping)
tips: Northern Chinese specialist — different from typical SF Cantonese
Bring shaobing into the meal — sandwich the lamb
Worth the drive from SF

restaurants.name: Joy Luck Place
restaurants.known_for: Standard dim sum spread. Strong egg tarts and turnip cakes.
restaurants.vibe: Less crowded alternative to Millbrae. Reliable.
tips: Less crowded than Millbrae spots
Egg tarts and turnip cakes are the strongest items
Reliable, not destination

restaurants.name: Din Tai Fung
restaurants.known_for: XLB (xiao long bao), truffle XLB, garlic green beans, shrimp & pork wontons.
restaurants.vibe: Reservation-based now. World-famous Taiwanese chain. Worth it.
tips: Reservations essential
Watch the dumpling-folders through the window — they're machines
Truffle XLB is luxury — the regular is just as good

restaurants.name: Hai Di Lao Hot Pot
restaurants.known_for: Service is the famous part — manicure while you wait, noodle dance, free snacks.
restaurants.vibe: Showy, fun, big group friendly. Hours-long wait without reservation.
tips: Free manicure during wait
Free fruit/snacks/games during wait
Show up an hour before reservation — half the fun is the waiting room

restaurants.name: Sichuan Home
restaurants.known_for: Authentic Sichuan — water-boiled fish, dan dan noodles, mapo tofu, twice-cooked pork.
restaurants.vibe: Strong heat. Order with respect.
tips: Heat is no joke — order rice
Call to ask spice level if you're unsure
Sichuan peppercorn is heavy — it numbs

restaurants.name: Liang's Kitchen
restaurants.known_for: Beef noodle soup, scallion pancakes, three-cup chicken, popcorn chicken.
restaurants.vibe: Casual Taiwanese cafe. Lunch crowd of tech workers.
tips: Casual lunch spot — quick service
Three-cup chicken is the underrated order
Bubble tea actually solid

restaurants.name: Chef Chu's
restaurants.known_for: Old-school Chinese-American fine — Peking duck, kung pao, walnut prawns.
restaurants.vibe: Founded 1970. Steve Jobs ate here. Family-run institution.
tips: Founded 1970
Steve Jobs ate here regularly
Family-run institution — old-school Chinese-American done right

restaurants.name: Joy Luck Palace
restaurants.known_for: South Bay dim sum — har gow, siu mai, BBQ pork buns. Carts at peak.
restaurants.vibe: Big Cantonese banquet hall. Reliable South Bay dim sum.
tips: Carts at peak weekend hours
Big banquet hall — fits big groups
Cheap relative to dim sum elsewhere

restaurants.name: Spicy King
restaurants.known_for: Boiled fish in chili oil, ma po tofu, dry-fried string beans. Heavy on the heat.
restaurants.vibe: South Bay Sichuan specialist. Order water with bread.
tips: Fremont Sichuan specialist
Heat is no joke — bring tolerant company
Order rice and water generously

restaurants.name: Champagne Seafood Restaurant
restaurants.known_for: Live tank seafood, lobster noodles, salt-and-pepper everything. Banquet-style.
restaurants.vibe: South Bay Cantonese banquet hall. Loud, big tables.
tips: Order from the tank for best price
South Bay Cantonese banquet vibe
Bring a group — lobster is the play

restaurants.name: Tasty Pot
restaurants.known_for: Individual hot pots, customizable broth and ingredients.
restaurants.vibe: Walk-in friendly alternative to Hai Di Lao.
tips: Walk-in friendly alternative to Hai Di Lao
Individual pot per person — no shared broth wars
Cheaper than Hai Di Lao

restaurants.name: Frank Fat's
restaurants.known_for: Banana cream pie (yes really), honey walnut prawns, classic Cantonese-American.
restaurants.vibe: Capitol institution since 1939. Lobbyists, legislators, tradition.
tips: Capitol institution since 1939
The pie is the surprise destination order
Order in the bar room for the old-Sacramento vibe

restaurants.name: Hunan Home's
restaurants.known_for: Crispy chicken with garlic sauce, hot braised fish, smoked pork.
restaurants.vibe: Chinatown Hunan classic. Less hyped, consistently solid.
tips: Less hyped than Z&Y but consistently solid
Hunan ≠ Sichuan — different heat profile, more chili less numbing
Try the smoked pork — distinct Hunan technique

restaurants.name: Tao Yuen Pastry
restaurants.known_for: Pork buns, taro buns, savory pastries. Bakery-style takeout.
restaurants.vibe: Counter service, cash, fast turnover. Cheap snacks for the road.
tips: Cash works, counter service, fast
Cheap snacks for the road
Buy a dozen — eat while driving

restaurants.name: 85°C Bakery Cafe
restaurants.signature_dish: Sea salt coffee + brioche pineapple bun
tips: Pull a tray, point at what you want, pay at the counter
Pastries pulled hourly — the late evening batch is fresher than mid-afternoon
The sea salt coffee is the chain's signature — get it
restaurants.known_for: Sea salt coffee + the Taiwanese-style pineapple bun. Pastries pulled hourly, lines move fast.
restaurants.vibe: Buzzing bakery counter. Open late, packed all day.

restaurants.name: Sheng Kee Bakery
tips: Counter service — point and pay
Open early, fresh batches all day
Cake by the slice in back
restaurants.known_for: Hong Kong–style bakery chain. Cocktail buns and BBQ pork buns are the staples.
restaurants.vibe: Counter service, fast turnover. The bakery half of any Milpitas Square run.

restaurants.name: Tea Era
tips: Customize sugar level (try 50%)
Fresh boba — they cook it through the day
Late-night boba spot
restaurants.known_for: Solid Taiwanese boba chain. Brown sugar boba is the destination order.
restaurants.vibe: Quick boba stop. Standing-room only at peak.

restaurants.name: Quickly
tips: Get the popcorn chicken with the basil garnish — that's the move
Combo with boba is the cheap dinner play
Fast counter service
restaurants.known_for: Old-school Taiwanese boba chain. Popcorn chicken is the food order.
restaurants.vibe: Counter service, plastic chairs. The OG boba experience.

restaurants.name: Boiling Hot Pot
tips: Split-pot is the play — mala on one side, mushroom on the other
All-you-can-eat option exists at lunch — plan accordingly
Bring layers — they crank the AC
restaurants.known_for: Solid mid-tier hot pot. Split-pot mala is the order. AYCE at lunch.
restaurants.vibe: Big group friendly. Loud. Long waits on weekends.

restaurants.name: Ten Ren's Tea
tips: Loose-leaf tea bar in the back — get a flight
Buy tea by the can to take home
Boba here uses better-than-average tea base
restaurants.known_for: Old-school Taiwanese tea house. Loose-leaf oolong + boba made with real tea.
restaurants.vibe: Quiet tea-shop counter. Smells like roasted oolong.

restaurants.name: Sang Kee Congee Noodle House
tips: Pair the congee with you tiao (fried dough)
Open early — breakfast destination
Low-key, no fuss
restaurants.known_for: Cantonese congee + wonton noodles. Breakfast comfort.
restaurants.vibe: Quiet, old-school noodle shop. Solo-friendly.

restaurants.name: Chef Liu Hand-Made Noodles
tips: Watch them pull noodles in the open kitchen
Order the spicy beef variant if you can take heat
Cash works
restaurants.known_for: Northern Chinese hand-pulled noodles, made fresh in the open kitchen.
restaurants.vibe: Tiny, packed at lunch. Watch the noodle-puller through the window.

restaurants.name: Mango Mango Dessert
tips: Late-night dessert spot — open till 11pm+
Shaved ice is enormous — share
Durian pancakes are the polarizing order
restaurants.known_for: HK-style mango shaved ice + sago desserts. The end-of-meal stop at Milpitas Square.
restaurants.vibe: Bright, casual dessert café. Date-night and end-of-meal crowd.

restaurants.name: Verde Tea Cafe
restaurants.signature_dish: Honey green tea + popcorn chicken combo
tips: Sit-down Taiwanese cafe — lunch combos are the value
Tea quality above the typical chain
Quieter than the boba spots up front
restaurants.known_for: Sit-down Taiwanese cafe — lunch combos with quality tea.
restaurants.vibe: Brighter, calmer than the boba shops. Solo and small-group friendly.

milpitas-square.name: Milpitas Square
milpitas-square.subtitle: Justin's favorite Chinese food destination in NorCal
milpitas-square.description: Asian shopping plaza anchored by 99 Ranch Market, on Milpitas Blvd between Calaveras and Yosemite. Bakeries, boba, hot pot, dessert spots and noodle houses all in one parking lot.
milpitas-square.tagline: 💫 Click any restaurant to dig in.
milpitas-square.the_move: Park once. Start at 85°C for a sea salt coffee + bun. Hit Quickly for popcorn chicken. Sit down for hot pot. End at Mango Mango for shaved ice.
